partial_design: Preserve O_append_predecessor_retention and bindings BIND_append_predecessor_retention and BIND_last_entry_retention. Use a TestAssurance-prefixed Go test in package raft. Initialize actual InmemStore entries (1,1) and (2,2), matching cached last-log metadata, current term 3, and zero commit and snapshot boundaries. Wrap the store so DeleteRange executes the actual implementation and records its outcome, while the following StoreLogs injects an error without writing. Invoke actual appendEntries synchronously with predecessor (1,1) and replacement LogNoop (2,3), then capture its completed response through a buffered RPC response channel. Independently inspect retained storage and cached metadata. Invoke the same receiver with term 3, predecessor (2,2), no entries, and no commitment advancement; capture its actual response and final retained-history observations. The independent safety oracle asserts Success=false only where observed lookup establishes absence of the requested predecessor and observed snapshot metadata establishes no snapshot representation. Other lookup errors remain unknown. Success is never an applicability filter. Correlate the initialization, successful deletion, injected storage failure, first completion, second input, and independent second result using stable fixture and operation identities and explicit causal references. Include a separate retained-predecessor control, recording completion and actual response without requiring success as a safety property. Actual synchronous calls and buffered RPC responses control receiver-local ordering and completion; they do not establish actor-dispatch or sender reachability. Disclose explicit initialization, direct handler invocation, the storage fault wrapper, and any address-codec substitute. Preserve exclusions concerning legal sender histories, intervening actor behavior, production adapter failure semantics, remote interpretation, and broader consensus consequences. These reads concern fixture dependencies within the existing unit; no additional protocol producer or filter is proposed.
